A32-603.summary: Schoning's secret mission at the Prussian court for Princess Wilhelmina: his arrival and the false patriots at Potsdam, Thulemeier 'un infame' and Hertzberg to be sent away, the King's hatred of the Prince and love of the Princess, a plan for a defensive and offensive alliance of the Republic with France, Spain and Prussia against England and the Emperor, his secret channel, and Gaffron's affair at Constantinople.
A32-603.en:
No. 1, 28 July 1783. I have the honour to inform you that I arrived yesterday on Prussian territory without the
slightest unfortunate accident, except that I am a little unwell ... This town is full of Dutchmen, among whom there
are some false patriots ... [I] told him to give well-deserved praise to the reigning burgomasters of Amsterdam. I
arrived in time to stop him doing the contrary, for the duke's party had [tried to undo] the good they have just
done. He is furiously worked up, that is, the ill humour he speaks of against Monsieur Thulemeier; he gives him no
pardon; but I told him to keep calm on this subject and to be very cautious for some time, for fear that he might
lack well-intentioned agents ... He suspected Monsieur your brother the general of belonging to the party of the
[...]; [...] to undeceive him ... before one is quite sure of success ... [Her Royal Highness] ...

snip.cap: No. 3, Potsdam 8 August 1783: symbol cipher with underlined code numbers (914 Thulemeier, 446 Hertzberg, 818 the King, 724 the Prince, 734 the Princess)

system: Letter signs (invented hook-and-stroke shapes, one per letter, a few homophones; a dot above doubles a letter; j = i) for running text, and 2-3 digit code numbers for names and titles.
